questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect option regarding mitochondria.
options: Inner membrane infolded to form cristae
Many circular DNA and few ribosomes found in matrix
questions.solution: Each mitochondrion is a double membrane-bound structure with the outer membrane and the inner membrane dividing its lumen distinctly into two aqueous compartments, i.e., the outer compartment and the inner compartment. The inner compartment is filled with fluid called matrix. The inner membrane forms a number of infoldings called the cristae. Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called 'power houses' of the cell. The matrix possesses single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (70S) etc.

questions.solution:
For the reaction, $2 \mathrm{NH}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{N}_2+3 \mathrm{H}_2$

From equation (i) and (ii)
$\therefore$ Rate of production of $\mathrm{N}_2, \frac{d\left[\mathrm{~N}_2\right]}{d t}=k=2.5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{~L}^{-1} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ From equation (iii) Rate of production of $\mathrm{H}_2, \frac{d\left[\mathrm{H}_2\right]}{d t}=3 k\begin{aligned} & =3 \times 2.5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1} \mathrm{~s}^{-1} \\ & =7.5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For a first order gas phase reaction,
$A_{(g)} \longrightarrow 2 B_{(g)}+C_{(g)}P_0$ be initial pressure of $A$ and $P_t$ the total pressure at time ' $t$ '. Integrated rate equation is
questions.solution: Total pressure at time $t=P_0-P+2 P+P=P_t\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow P_t=P_0+2 P \\ & P_t-P_0=2 P \Rightarrow P=\frac{P_t-P_0}{2} \\ & k=\frac{2.303}{t} \log \left[\frac{P_0}{P_0-P}\right] \\ & =\frac{2.303}{t} \log \left[\frac{P_0}{P_0-\left(\frac{P_t-P_0}{2}\right)}\right] \\ & =\frac{2.303}{t} \log \left[\frac{2 P_0}{2 P_0-P_t+P_0}\right]=\frac{2.303}{t} \log \left[\frac{2 P_0}{3 P_0-P_t}\right]\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry

For a first order reaction,
$\begin{aligned} & k=\frac{2.303}{t} \log \frac{a}{a-x} \\ & \therefore \quad t=\frac{2.303}{4.3 \times 10^{-4}} \log \frac{a}{a / 3}=2.55 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element germanium crystallises in $b c c$ type crystal structure with edge of unit cell equal to $288 \mathrm{pm}$ and the density of the element equal to $7.2 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$. The number of atoms present in $52 \mathrm{~g}$ of the crystalline element and the atomic mass of the element are respectively
questions.solution:
$d=7.2 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}, a=288 \mathrm{pm}$ and mass of element $=52 \mathrm{~g}$
Hence, $d=\frac{\text { Mass }}{\text { Volume }} \Rightarrow 7.2 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}=\frac{52 \mathrm{~g}}{V}V=\frac{52 \mathrm{~g}}{7.2 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}}=7.222 \mathrm{~cm}^3$
Edge of unit cell, $a=288 \mathrm{pm}=288 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{~m}=288 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~cm}=2.88 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~cm}$
Volume of unit cell, $a^3=\left(2.88 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~cm}\right)^3=23.888 \times 10^{-24} \mathrm{~cm}^3$
The number of unit cells in $52 \mathrm{~g}$ of metal
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{\text { Total volume }}{\text { Volume of one unit cell }} \\ & =\frac{7.222 \mathrm{~cm}^3}{23.888 \times 10^{-24} \mathrm{~cm}^3}=0.3023 \times 10^{24}\end{aligned}$
Germanium has body centred cubic structure. Hence, its unit cell contains 2 atoms.
$\therefore$ Total atoms in $3.023 \times 10^{23}$ unit cells are $2 \times 3.023 \times 10^{23}=6.046 \times 10^{23}$ atoms
Molar mass $=\frac{52 \mathrm{~g} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} \text { atom } \mathrm{mol}^{-1}}{6.046 \times 10^{23} \text { atom }}$
Hence, atomic mass $=51.8$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Formula of metal oxide with metal deficiency defect in its crystal is $A_{0.8} \mathrm{O}$. The crystal contains $A^{2+}$ and $A^{3+}$ ions. The fraction of metal existing as $A^{2+}$ ions in the crystal is
questions.solution:
$A: \mathrm{O}=0.8: 1=80: 100$
Thus, if there are $100 \mathrm{O}$ atoms, then number of $A$ atoms $=80$
Charge on $100 \mathrm{O}^{2-}$ ions $=100 \times(-2)=-200$
Suppose number of $A$ atoms present as $A^{2+}=x\therefore \quad$ Number of $\mathrm{A}$ atoms present as $A^{3+}=80-x$
Total charge on $A^{2+}$ and $A^{3+}=x \times(+2)+(80-x) \times(+3)=2 x+240-3 x=240-x$
As metal oxide is neutral,
Total charge on cations $=$ total charge on anions
$\therefore \quad 240-x=200$ or $x=40\therefore \quad$ Fraction of metal existing as $A^{2+}$ ions in the crystal $=40 / 80=0.5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Reaction, $A \rightleftharpoons B+3 C$ at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is in equilibrium. If equilibrium constant and Gibbs' free energy for this reaction are $y$ and $x$ respectively, then the Gibbs' free energy for reaction, $\frac{1}{2} A \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2} B+\frac{3}{2} C$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathbf{} A \rightleftharpoons B+3 C \\ & K=\frac{[B][C]^3}{[A]} \\ & \Delta G^{\circ}=-R T \ln K=x\end{aligned}$
For the reaction, $\frac{1}{2} A \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2} B+\frac{3}{2} C\begin{aligned} & K^{\prime}=\frac{[B]^{1 / 2}[C]^{3 / 2}}{[A]^{1 / 2}} \quad \text { or } \quad\left(K^{\prime}\right)^2=\frac{[B][C]^3}{[A]}=K \\ & \Delta G_2^{\circ}=-R T \ln K^{\prime}=-R T \ln \sqrt{K} \\ & =-\frac{1}{2} R T \ln K=\frac{x}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance $9 \mathrm{nF}$ having dielectric slab of $\varepsilon_r=2.4$, dielectric strength $20 \mathrm{MV} \mathrm{m}^{-1}$, and potential difference $=20 \mathrm{~V}$. Calculate area of plates.
questions.solution:
Here, $C=9 \mathrm{nF}, \varepsilon_r=2.4, V=20$ volt
Dielectric strength $=20 \mathrm{MV} \mathrm{m}^{-1}$
Let separation between plates $=d\begin{aligned} & E=\frac{V}{d} \Rightarrow 20 \times 10^6=\frac{20}{d} \\ & d=10^{-6} \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$
Now, $C=\frac{\varepsilon_0 A \varepsilon_r}{d}\begin{aligned} & 9 \times 10^{-9}=\frac{8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times A \times 2.4}{10^{-6}} \\ & A=\frac{9 \times 10^{-15}}{8.85 \times 2.4 \times 10^{-12}}=4.2 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2\end{aligned}$

Energy transferred to $B$.

Final velocity of
$\begin{aligned} & v_B=\left(\frac{m_2-m_1}{m_1+m_2}\right) u_2+\frac{2 m_1 u_1}{m_1+m_2} \\ & m_1=4 m, u_1=u \\ & m_2=2 m, u_2=0 \\ & v_B=\frac{2(4 m) u}{6 m}=\frac{4}{3} u \\ & \frac{\frac{1}{2} m_2 v_B^2}{\frac{1}{2} m_1 u_1^2}=\frac{\frac{1}{2} 2 m\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^2 u^2}{\frac{1}{2} 4 m u^2} \\ & \end{aligned}$
Fraction of energy lost $=8 / 9$

questions.q: Four point charges $-Q,-q, 2 q$ and $2 Q$ are placed, one at each corner of the square. The relation between $Q$ and $q$ for which the potential at the centre of the square is zero is
questions.solution: Let $a$ be the side length of the square $A B C D$. $\begin{aligned} & A C=B D=\sqrt{a^2+a^2}=a \sqrt{2} \\ & O A=O B=O C=O D=\frac{a \sqrt{2}}{2}=\frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$ Potential is a scalar quantity. Hence, the force of friction between $A$ and $B$ is zero.

questions.q: A potential difference $V=100 \pm 5 \mathrm{~V}$, when applied across a resistance, gives a current $I=10 \pm 0.2 \mathrm{~A}$. What is the percentage error in $R$ ?
questions.solution:
Potential difference is $V=100 \pm 5 \mathrm{~V}$
Current is $I=10 \pm 0.2 \mathrm{~A}$.
Percentage error in voltage is obtained as
$\frac{\Delta V}{V}=\frac{5}{100} \times 100 \%=5 \%$
Percentage error in current is obtained as
$\frac{\Delta I}{I}=\frac{0.2}{10} \times 100 \%=2 \%$
Using, $R=\frac{V}{I}$, the percentage error in resistance is calculated as $R=5 \%+2 \%=7 \%$.

$a=\frac{F}{m_1+m_2}$

questions.q: Pancreatic juice/enzyme digests
options: triglycerides, proteins and nucleic acids only
nucleic acids, proteins, fat and starch.
questions.solution: The exocrine part of the pancreas consists of rounded lobules (acini) that secrete an alkaline pancreatic juice with $\mathrm{pH}$ 8.4. The pancreatic juice is carried by the main pancreatic duct into the duodenum through the hepatopancreatic ampulla. The accessory pancreatic duct directly pours the pancreatic juice into the duodenum. The pancreatic juice contains sodium bicarbonate, three proenzymes; trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen and procarboxypeptidase and some enzymes such as elastase, pancreatic $\alpha$-amylase, DNase, RNase and pancreatic lipase. The pancreatic juice helps in the digestion of starch, proteins, fats and nucleic acids.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which vitamin is associated with the maintenance of bone density?
questions.solution: Bone density is the amount of bone mineral present in bone tissue. The higher the bone mineral content, the denser the bones are. Several vitamins are important to bone health. Vitamin $\mathrm{B}_{12}$ has an effect on bone building cells. The low levels of $\mathrm{B}_{12}$ result in the higher risk of osteoporosis in both men and women and thus results in lower bone density. Vitamin $\mathrm{C}$ is essential for the formation of collagen, the foundation that bone mineralization is built on. Increased levels of vitamin $\mathrm{C}$ results in greater bone density. Vitamin D is most essential for greater bone density. It helps the body to absorb calcium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the function of Bowman's capsule and Glomerulus?
questions.solution: The renal tubule begins with a double walled cup-like structure called Bowman's capsule which encloses the glomerulus. Glomerulus along with Bowman's capsule is called the Malpighian body or renal corpuscle. The first step in urine formation is the filtration of blood, which is carried out by the glomerulus and is called glomerular filtration. The glomerular capillary blood pressure causes filtration of blood through 3 layers, i.e., the endothelium of glomerular blood vessels, the epithelium of Bowman's capsule and a basement membrane between these two layers. The epithelial cells of Bowman's capsule called podocytes are arranged in an intricate manner so as to leave some minute spaces called filtration slits or slit pores. Blood is filtered so finely through these membranes, that almost all the constituents of the plasma except the proteins pass onto the lumen of the Bowman's capsule.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Acidic $\mathrm{pH}$ of muscles is due to
questions.solution: Lactic acid is formed and accumulated in the muscle under conditions of high energy demand, rapid fluctuations of the energy requirement and insufficient supply of $\mathrm{O}_2$. This results in acidic $\mathrm{pH}$ of muscle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Who discovered DNA fingerprinting?
questions.solution: DNA-fingerprinting (also called DNA profiling) is a technique of determining nucleotide sequences of certain areas of DNA which are unique to each individual. Alec Jeffreys in 1984 invented the DNA fingerprinting technique at Leicester University, United Kingdom.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The group of codons which codes for alanine is
questions.solution: GCU, GCC, GCA and GCG code for alanine. GAU and GAC code for aspartine while GAA codes for glutamine. AGU and AGC code for serine, AGA codes for arginine whereas GUU, GUC and GUA code for valine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Assertion : In eukaryotes, both intron and exon are transcribed to form hnRNA.
Reason : Splicing is required in prokaryotes.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Eukaryotic transcripts possess extra segments called introns or intervening sequences or non-coding sequences. They do not appear in mature or processed RNA. The functional coding sequences are called exons. Splicing is removal of introns and fusion of exons to form functional RNAs. Splicing is generally not required in prokaryotes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement for autonomic nervous system.
options: Transmit impulse from CNS to involuntary organs
Consists of sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system
questions.solution: The autonomic neural system controls and coordinates involuntary activities of various organs. It transmits impulses from the CNS to the involuntary organs and smooth muscles of the body. The autonomic neural system is further classified into sympathetic neural system and parasympathetic neural system.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Assertion : Fig and wasp cannot complete their life cycle without each other.
Reason : They show mutualistic relationship.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: In many species of fig trees, there is a tight one-to-one relationship with the pollinator species of wasp. It means that a given fig species can be pollinated only by its 'partner' wasp species and no other species. The female wasp uses the fruit not only as an oviposition (egg-laying) site but uses the developing seeds within the fruit for nourishing its larvae. The wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence while searching for suitable egg-laying sites. In return for the favour of pollination the fig offers the wasp some of its developing seeds, as food for the developing wasp larvae.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Identify the given diagram of tissue performing secretion and absorption.
questions.solution: The given figure is of simple cuboidal epithelium. The cells are cubical and more or less squarish in shape. In surface view, the cells appear polygonal. The nuclei are rounded and lie in the centre of the cells. The cuboidal epithelium is present in the small salivary and pancreatic ducts, thyroid follicles, parts of membranous labyrinth, etc.
